title: fix(cloud-connection): every replica reads the cloud binding credential when several are declared
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HPKXhgTmBFYjXgTdNcFMFqGb)_

Closes #31554

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**：声明多副本（`OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS` 大于 1 或 `OS_EXPECT_MULTI_NODE=true`）并且集群驱动是 Redis 时，云绑定凭据改存数据库里的一行加密记录（`sys_cloud_binding_credential`），所有副本读写同一行；另提供一个内核启动前的一次性读取，供启动前的多节点许可证检查使用。单机和其他驱动继续用原来的文件，路径、字节和权限都不变。
- **为什么改**：凭据原来只存在执行绑定那台副本的本地文件里，其余副本拿不到凭据，在线许可证检查报告没有控制平面，对云端的调用也不带凭据。
- **风险与回滚**：只在上面两个条件同时成立时生效，单机路径有逐字节回归测试；没有加密提供者时拒绝绑定，不会明文落库；启动前读取有 3 秒上限，失败时按未绑定启动，不会卡住启动。回滚即撤回本 PR，多副本部署会回到各自读文件（需要重新绑定一次）。
- **先看**：`packages/cloud-connection/src/cloud-connection-plugin.ts`（`chooseLedger`、`door` 包装、bind/poll 写入失败分支）、`connection-credential-preboot.ts`（启动前读取的超时与关闭）、`connection-credential-ledger.ts`（读写、`adoptFrom` 迁移）。
- **两分钟验证**：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cloud-connection exec vitest run src/connection-credential-ledger.test.ts src/connection-credential-store.test.ts src/connection-credential-preboot.test.ts`，预期 38 个用例全绿，其中双进程用例显示 A 绑定后 B 立即带上凭据、A 解绑后 B 立即清空。
- **需要你做的**：无，席位落地。

## What changes

A self-hosted server kept its cloud binding credential only in the working directory's `.objectstack/cloud-connection.json`. Under several replicas, the bind ran on one replica and every other replica held no credential.

- **New object `sys_cloud_binding_credential`** (`packages/cloud-connection`): one row, keyed by `slot = 'runtime'` under a global unique index. `runtime_token` is a `Field.secret`, so the engine seals it through the host `ICryptoProvider` into `sys_secret` (fail-closed with no provider), masks it on read and releases the handle on update or delete. The object is engine-owned, tenant-free (`systemFields.tenant: false`), `apiEnabled: false`, with `maxLength` on every text column.
- **Where the credential lives is chosen once, in `init()`**, by `sharesCloudBindingCredential(env, driver)`: the shared row exactly when `declaresMultiNode(env)` holds (service-cluster's predicate, the one the entitlement half in cloud#3880 reads) and the cluster driver is `redis` (`CLOUD_BINDING_SHARED_CLUSTER_DRIVER`, per cloud#3814 R2/R3). Anything else, including any other driver, keeps the file through `fileCredentialLedger`, a pass-through over the unchanged `ConnectionCredentialStore`. The object is registered with the `manifest` service only on the shared path.
- **Reads**: on shared replicas every `/api/v1/cloud-connection/*` door re-reads the row before it runs. The synchronous `cloud-binding` service answers from a copy read at `kernel:ready` and re-read every 30 s (`sharedCredentialRefreshMs`). A new `cloud-binding-credential` service exposes an async `load()` that reads the row on demand, for readers that can await (the EE licence check, after a pin).
- **Writes**: bind and unbind write that one row from any replica. Unbind keeps the `runtimeId` residual, the same shape the file keeps. On shared replicas a credential that cannot be sealed is refused to the caller with `503 ENVIRONMENT_BIND_FAILED` and a message that names the fix, instead of answering the bind as connected. The single node answers as before.
- **Before the kernel**: `readCloudBindingCredentialBeforeBoot({ openDriver, cryptoProvider })` is for the host's config, ahead of the multi-node licence gate, so a cold cluster can make its first-boot exchange. It opens nothing unless the predicate above holds (reading `OS_CLUSTER_DRIVER`, or a `clusterDriver` the host passes). Otherwise it opens the one driver the host supplies and reads the row through a bare ObjectQL engine with only this object registered. That is the same `load()` the plugin uses, so the secret is dereferenced by the engine's `resolveSecretField` and nothing else. It runs no schema sync and no write. It initiates the disconnect on every path, including an open that lands after the bound. Open, read and close share one deadline; the close is waited for only with what is left (at least 50 ms), and on the timeout path it is initiated, not awaited (`timeoutMs`, default `PREBOOT_CREDENTIAL_TIMEOUT_MS` = 3000). Any failure answers `{ status: 'unavailable', reason }` and never throws, so the replica boots as an unbound one does today.
- **Migration of an existing file**: the first shared boot moves the file's credential into the row when the row is empty and logs the path. The file is left in place and not read while replicas are declared. Scaling back to one replica reads the file again; it does not follow binds made meanwhile, so the docs say to disconnect and connect again after scaling down.
- **Logging**: the credential is never logged, and the ledger scrubs it from any engine error it re-throws. One `error` line, with consequence and fix, when replicas are declared over Redis with no `manifest` service (each replica keeps its own file), when the move fails, and when a shared read fails (once per distinct failure).
- **Ledgers the new object needs**: `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` in `@objectstack/spec`, the organization ownership inventory row in `@objectstack/cli`, and the regenerated `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`.
- **Docs**: `content/docs/deployment/cloud-connection.mdx` gains "Several replicas".

## Why the database row and not the cluster KV

- The binding is a durable secret and the system of record. The `IKV` contract says it is not a database, customer Redis may run without persistence, and a flush must never disconnect the server.
- The row inherits the engine's secret-field seam: encryption at rest with the platform crypto provider, masking on read, handle release, and a fail-closed refusal without a provider. A KV entry would need its own encryption and has none of that.
- No pubsub invalidation lane: the repo's rule is that the re-read interval is the correctness bound and pubsub is only a hint. The doors re-read on every request, so the only window is the synchronous service's 30 s.
- The PM thread confirmed this route. The sibling cloud#3869 keeps its entitlement cache in KV with a file fallback, by design.

## Tests

- **Two processes** (`connection-credential-ledger.test.ts`): two real Node processes, each with its own working directory and credential file, boot `CloudConnectionPlugin` from this checkout's source over one SQLite database file and one crypto key, with `OS_CLUSTER_REPLICAS=2` and the Redis cluster driver. A binds through its door. B's next door presents the same bearer to a local control plane at once, and B's synchronous service has it within the re-read interval. A unbinds, and B reads not connected without calling the control plane, keeping the `runtimeId` residual. Neither replica writes a credential file, the database file never holds the bearer in plaintext, and neither replica's logs or stderr contain it.
- **Single node byte-identical** (`connection-credential-store.test.ts`, four topologies: no declaration over Redis, replicas declared over `memory`, replicas declared over `postgres`, replicas declared with no cluster service): bind/poll writes the exact bytes the store wrote before this change, mode `0600`; nothing is registered with the manifest service; the reader answers from the file; unbind leaves `{ runtimeToken: '', runtimeId }`.
- **Ledger over a real engine** (6 cases): round-trip with no plaintext at rest; residual and rotation; a replica on another key refuses and names `OS_SECRET_KEY`; no crypto provider refuses; no data engine refuses; the file moves into the empty row once and never over a filled one.
- **Plugin** (3 cases): the shared path registers the object, says so once and moves the file before the first door; no manifest service logs one `error` and keeps the file; a bind the row cannot seal answers 503 and stores nothing.
- **Pre-boot read** (`connection-credential-preboot.test.ts`, 16 cases, including three that pin the one shared deadline: a hung open, a slow open with a hung close, a hung read with a hung close): a real SQLite file sealed by a replica's engine is read back through a fresh driver and the same key, then disconnected; nothing bound reads as `null`; a host-supplied `clusterDriver` is honoured. A database that never held the row, another key, an open that throws, an open that lands after the bound (answered at the bound, closed when it lands) and a hung read (closed at the bound) are each `unavailable` without throwing, with no credential in the reason. No declaration, `memory`, no driver, `postgres` and an unknown driver each answer `not-shared` without calling `openDriver`.
- **Ablations** (each restored by `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, blob equal to HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty): forcing `chooseLedger` to return the file ledger turns the two-process case red (`expected '' to be 'oscc_dummy_31554_aaaa'`); removing the shared bind refusal turns its case red (`expected 200 to be 503`); widening the predicate to any non-`memory` driver turns the three non-Redis cases red; dropping the close on the success path turns the four disconnect assertions red.

## Acceptance notes

- **File surface beyond the claim.** The claim names `packages/cloud-connection/**` and the object that holds the row. The diff also touches `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts` and `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`, because their conformance tests fail for any new platform object not listed; plus the docs page, the changeset and `pnpm-lock.yaml` for the new workspace dependencies.
- **Residual, not touched:** `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` builds its own `ConnectionCredentialStore` and reads the file for install-local's control-plane fetch. Install-local under several replicas is ruled to refuse loudly on a separate card, so this PR leaves it reading the file it read before.
- **Cloud half:** after the next pin bump, the host's `objectstack.config.ts` calls `readCloudBindingCredentialBeforeBoot` with its datasource driver and crypto provider ahead of the multi-node gate, and the running licence check reads `cloud-binding-credential` or the `cloud-binding` service.
- **Out of scope:** moving the single node's file under `OS_HOME` (today it sits in the container layer) is a separate single-node bug that the maintainer is being asked about.
- **Test budget:** the three credential suites together take about 7 s of test time locally, under the 10 s line per file, so no budget header.

## Verification

All readings at head `786e5d7b`.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cloud-connection exec vitest run`: Test Files 79 passed (79), Tests 1081 passed (1081).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cloud-connection typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit` and `tsconfig.test.json`): clean, after a declaration build of the dependency closure.
- `@objectstack/spec` `platform-object-names`, `api-methods-batch-conformance` and `platform-tool-names` tests: 23/23. `@objectstack/cli` `organization-ownership-inventory` test: 26/26.
- `eslint` on every changed source and test file: clean.

<details><summary>Derived gate union (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`): 137 commands, 133 exit 0, 4 NOT MEASURED</summary>

- 125 exit 0 in one pass. The `@objectstack/spec` gates were then rerun one at a time after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` (declarations on), because this diff edits a spec source file: all 18 exit 0, including `check:api-surface`, `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface`.
- `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exited 3 on the shallow checkout (its fixture commit was missing). It exits 0 after fetching that one commit.
- Fixed during the run: `check:engine-double-contract` (the new in-process engine fake now opens `update`/`delete` with the dispatch asserts; ledger re-recorded with `--write`) and `check:logger-receiver-detach` (the three `error` lines go through one receiver-safe helper).
- NOT MEASURED, reason: prerequisite not met (exit 3), because they need a whole-workspace build or the built CLI. These are `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage` and `check:i18n-walk-parity`. CI runs all four.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran`: 137 derived, 137 run.

</details>

## Human Minimum

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic.
- [x] 2. Every name I added uses the casing for its kind.
- [x] 3. No formatter ran; `eslint` passes on the changed files (the repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's run).
- [x] 4. One issue, one branch off an up-to-date `main`, one pull request.
- [x] 5. A change that publishes carries a changeset, and both declaration lines are filled in here and in the changeset.
- [x] 6. `packages/spec` touched: its generated artifacts are regenerated and committed.
- [x] 7. No hand edits to `content/docs/references/`, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` or `content/docs/releases/`.
- [ ] 8. Title, body and comments are in English. (The 维护者速读 block is Chinese by the dispatch contract.)
- [ ] The *Before Submitting* list in CONTRIBUTING.md is done.
